--- page 3 ---
Narrative text, no figure. Section 1 Introduction: Pacific vulnerability to climate hazards, OCHA 2023-2026 Strategic Plan commitment to anticipatory action, March 2023 Pacific AA Week in Nadi, RC request and USG/ERC approval for Fiji pilot with pre-arranged CERF financing. Subsection "Coordination with local authorities": National Disaster Management Act 1998, NDMO role, framework developed with NDMO (Sept 2023) and endorsed by National Disaster Management Council; trigger/activation protocol designed with Fiji Meteorological Service (FMS) and NDMO.

--- page 4 ---
Map/diagram: "Fiji Humanitarian Coordination Structure" (as of 02 November 2023). Org chart shows Cabinet (PM) → National Disaster Management Council (Minister of Rural & Maritime Dev & Disaster Mgmt) → National Disaster Controller and Emergency Committee → NDMO/NEOC → 10 National Clusters (Logistics, Shelter, Food Security & Livelihood, Education, Communication, WASH, Safety and Protection, Health and Nutrition, Infrastructure) each with lead ministry and co-leads. Location Map (right side): Fiji archipelago showing Labasa, Lautoka, Levuka, Suva (national capital), Kadavu, Moala, Yagasa, Lau Group; 50 km scale bar; inset globe locating Fiji in Pacific Ocean. Below: "Risk/Hazard" text — since 1969, 33 TCs (Category 1+) passed within 10km of Fiji, 16 made landfall; cites Cyclone Winston (2016, strongest in Southern Hemisphere), Yasa (2020, 2nd-strongest landfall), Harold (2020); NDC estimates >6.5% of Fiji's GDP could be lost to TCs/floods by 2050, poverty push increasing 25%/year.

--- page 5 ---
Narrative text, no figure. Continuation citing Fiji's National Adaptation Plan (NAP) and National DRR policy identifying TCs as major climate hazard. "Anticipatory action" section: defines AA as acting ahead of predicted hazards using the model (triggers/decision rules), the delivery (activities), and the money (pre-arranged financing); includes documenting evidence/learning.

--- page 6 ---
Narrative text, no figure. Section 2 "The Model": RSMC Nadi (operated by Fiji Meteorological Services) is WMO-designated authority for TC forecasts equator-25°S, 160°E-120°W. Issues official 72-hour track forecasts + 5-day formation risk outlooks; framework uses 72-hour forecast for action trigger and unofficial 120-hour forecast for readiness trigger. "Trigger Conditions": Category 4 or 5 within 250km of Fiji, OR Category 3/4/5 making landfall in Fiji. 2-stage trigger: (1) Readiness trigger — any point in 120-hr forecast meets conditions; (2) Action trigger — any point up to 72-hr lead time meets conditions. Action trigger detection rate defined as 100%. "Trigger Monitoring Process" steps 1-3: 120-hr forecast produced by FMS Senior Scientific Officer; emailed as CSV to OCHA Centre for Humanitarian Data (data.science@humdata.org); automated script evaluates trigger conditions.

--- page 7 ---
Diagram: process flow chart of trigger monitoring, "Times are estimates based on TC bench schedule, for satellite info published at 06:00". Shows RSMC/FMS TC Bench → 07:00 publication of forecast image → FMS Public Site (already existing activity); 06:40 also sent to NDMO. Bench also sends 06:35 email of 120-hour forecast CSV and 06:40 email of 72-hour forecast CSV to OCHA CHD (automatic script), which at 06:40 emails trigger report to Distribution List A (RC, UN agencies, NDMO). Below: "Activation protocol" table with columns Who/What/How/When for RSMC Nadi/FMS, OCHA CHD, NDMO, CERF, RC (rows continue to next page) — describes each actor's role and timing in sending forecasts, evaluating triggers, disbursing CERF funds, and RC's ability to pause activation.

--- page 8 ---
Table continuation (NDMO pause row) plus text on geographic prioritization info email (sample in Annex 5). Diagram: "Tropical Cyclone Monitoring" timeline showing repeated FMS/NDMO/OCHA forecast cycles leading to Readiness notice (bell icon) then Activation notice (play icon) triggering CERF disbursement and a chain of Activities (icons: food, cash, health, WASH). Below diagram: alternate path showing NDMO/RC "Joint decision to pause the process" (pause icon) if forecast track suggests minimal impact. Text: any triggering should lead to action; RC in consultation with government may pause for outlier low-impact cases. "Challenges and potential improvements": need for impact-based forecasting, short lead times requiring more investment in cyclone forecasting science, TC hazard framework covers windspeed only (not rainfall/storm surge) — future exploration of rainfall-based AA and other hazards noted.

--- page 9 ---
Narrative text, no figure. Section 3 "The Activities": Overview — TCs impact vulnerable populations with short window of opportunity, remote/hard-to-access areas may mean action becomes ex-post. "Selection Criteria" for activities: 1) Anticipatory character, 2) Ability to deliver within window of opportunity, 3) Operational capacity, 4) No regrets approach. "Activity 1. Multi-Purpose Cash" (MWCSP/WFP, Safety and Protection Cluster): Objective mitigate impact on household food/nutrition security. Description: WFP + MWCSP support projected 15,000 households (75,000 people) with anticipatory unconditional cash transfers of FJD200 via Dept of Social Protection (DSP), channeled through 4 national social protection schemes (Family Assistance Scheme, Care and Protection Allowance, Disability Allowance, Social Pension Scheme).

--- page 10 ---
Narrative text, no figure. Continuation of Activity 1: Partners (MWCSP, Ministry of Finance); Challenges — social registry restricts targeting to existing beneficiaries, limited oversight on inclusion/exclusion errors, need for early action plans for horizontal expansion. "Activity 2. Fishing-boat strengthening kits and water-tight drums" (Ministry of Agriculture/FAO/Fijian Red Cross): Objective reduce loss of livelihoods (boats, tools, cash crops). Description: FAO + Fiji Red Cross distribute fishing-boat strengthening kits and water-tight drums to at-risk fisherfolk/farmers. Partners: Ministry of Agriculture, Fiji Red Cross, IFRC. Challenges: logistics/prepositioning items sourced mainly from Suva/Nadi, need for simulation exercises in off-season.

--- page 11 ---
Narrative text, no figure. "Activity 3. Maternal and reproductive health supplies and GBV protection" (MHMS, MWCSP, UNFPA): Objective safeguard health/well-being of women and girls. Description: clean delivery kits, dignity kits (women 15-49 incl. disabilities), menstrual hygiene kits (girls 10+). Partners listed. Challenges: data accuracy (MISP calculator), logistical constraints (pre-positioning), coordination/collaboration — each with bullet mitigation strategies. "Activity 4. Distribution of WASH kits" (MHMS/UNICEF): Objective mitigate impact on water/sanitation access and hygiene.

--- page 12 ---
Narrative text, no figure. Continuation Activity 4 WASH: bullet activities (cluster coordination, prepositioning WASH NFIs, gender/disability-sensitive support, M&E). Partners and challenges (training, contingency partnerships, LTAs with suppliers). "Activity 5. Learning materials" (Ministry of Education/UNICEF): school-in-a-box kits, PFA for children; partners MEHRD; challenges — lack of detailed school population/vulnerability data, tents sourced internationally with slow lead times, limited local tent-erection expertise. "Activity 6. Shelter strengthening kits" (Ministry of Rural & Maritime Development/IOM with IFRC support): Objective minimize shelter damage; description begins listing IEC materials, ropes/fasteners/tarpaulins, construction tools.

--- page 13 ---
Narrative text, no figure. Continuation Activity 6 Shelter: Partners (Ministry of Rural & Maritime Development, IOM, IFRC, Fiji Red Cross, Habitat for Humanity). Challenges: cost spikes after landfall risk under/over-support, limited capacity-building window, difficulty reaching maritime islands (stocks concentrated in Viti Levu/Vanua Levu, Suva/Nadi). "Activity 7. Safety and Protection horizontal support" (MWCSP/UN Women): rapid assessment via Kobo app, social welfare/women's interest officers; challenges — staff designation only at time of emergency, network/device limitations for Kobo data collection. "Activity 8. Health and Nutrition Cluster Coordination" (Ministry of Health/WHO): objective stated, description begins.

--- page 14 ---
Narrative text, no figure. Continuation Activity 8 Health/Nutrition: bullet activities (cluster coordination support, assessments/service delivery support, advocacy). Partners: MOH, Health and Nutrition Cluster, ADRA, Empower Pacific, IFRC, IPPF, SPC, Save the Children, UNFPA, UNICEF, WHO. Challenges: need for resilient health system. "Activity 9. Common approach to Early Warning and Community Sensitization" (UNICEF/UNDRR): builds on "Get Ready Disaster Happen" campaign; multi-channel (radio, TV, social media, SMS) messages in English/iTaukei/Hindi, frequency increases with activation trigger; Turaga ni Koros/village leaders engaged. Partners: Ministry of Rural & Maritime Dev, NDMO, Communication Cluster, UNDRR, WHO. Challenges: telecom disruption risk, restricted movement, need to revise messages. "Logistics" section begins: UNCT SharePoint, Long-Term Agreements (LTA) Directory, UN Mutual Recognition Agreement.

--- page 15 ---
Narrative text, no figure. Continuation Logistics: Access to LTA Directory, Mutual Recognition Statement, Global LTA Requests via UNGM, Piggybacking Process. "Challenges and potential improvements in the future" bullets: limited preparatory timeframe before 2023 season, common targeting approach being explored, common logistics under UNICEF/national Logistics cluster leadership, remote areas (Eastern division) hard to reach, TC unpredictable paths complicate targeting, data accuracy issues with national social protection registry, restricted access to at-risk peri-urban groups, need for local partner engagement.

--- page 16 ---
Narrative text, no figure. Continuation bullets: private sector collaboration (Fiji Disaster Business Resilience Council, OCHA/UNDP Connecting Business Initiative), need for timely response plans alongside AA plans, capacity-building investment for SRH/GBV responders, CERF-AA Framework ensuring protection of PWDs/marginalized groups per footnote 10 on Fiji's human rights treaty ratifications; OHCHR Pacific Regional Office proposed collaboration on HRBA/SDG integration.

--- page 18 ---
Narrative text, no figure. "Co-Financing" section: WFP received USD500,000 from German Federal Foreign Office (reaching 10,000 extra households; total 15,000 households target for MPC). FAO USD200,000 from German Federal Foreign Office for watertight drums/fishing boat kits with Fiji Red Cross. UNICEF USD400,000 from Global Humanitarian Thematic Funds. UNFPA additional 212,413 USD complementing 200,000 USD from USAID-BHA/DFAT. WHO co-financing for early warning message testing and Health/Nutrition Cluster support. UNW co-financing extends Information Management support to MWCSP from Core Humanitarian Funds. "Challenges" bullets begin: start-up/build costs not traditionally funded by pooled funds like CERF, limited emergency-preparedness funding limits framework scope, storms likely to exceed AA's targeted scope/reach.

--- page 19 ---
Narrative text, no figure. One-line continuation: need to ensure linkages between emergency response preparedness, anticipatory action, rapid response and early recovery (community engagement, activities, financing).

--- page 20 ---
Narrative text, no figure. Section 5 "The Learning": framework activation offers learning/evidence-generation opportunities; OCHA-convened M&E committee; two learning streams: 1) independent agency M&E, 2) multi-stakeholder/multi-disciplinary impact assessment of CERF pilot. Pre-identified learning question areas listed: Timing, Impact, Joint targeting, Social inclusion, Early warning, Localization, Partnership, Actions, Impact (socio-economic/ROI). "Monitoring & Evaluation" subsection: each agency uses existing M&E systems financed via CERF, coordinated questionnaires. "Independent Evaluation" subsection begins: agencies agree to participate in independent evaluation for cohesive impact narrative.

--- page 21 ---
Narrative text, no figure. Continuation Independent Evaluation: agency support activities (feedback on methodology, collect pre/post disaster data, share beneficiary data, support common surveys). Three evaluation scenarios due to late Framework finalization: Scenario A - AA triggered after Jan 2024 (time for baseline data collection); Scenario B - AA triggered before Jan 2024 (no time for baseline); Scenario C - no AA triggered during 2023/24 season until end April 2024. Evaluation covers 3 components: process learning, socio-economic household impacts, ROI calculations. Quasi-experimental difference-in-difference design proposed; FAO providing technical support via Asia Pacific Technical Working Group on AA (co-led with IFRC).

--- page 22 ---
Narrative text, no figure. Section 6 "Final provisions" — Advocacy and public communication: agencies coordinate key messages under NDMO/RC leadership; activation triggers joint press release (Annex 8) and mutual social media amplification; sharing of visuals/impact stories with ad hoc committee.

--- page 23 ---
Narrative text, no figure. Annex 1 "Trigger Evaluation Specification": Category based on Australian TC intensity scale from RSMC Nadi forecast. Official forecast max lead time 72 hours (part of full 120-hour forecast used for readiness trigger only); 120-hour forecast not publicly available, 72-hour truncated version is published. Landfall/distance determined via "best track" forecast, linear interpolation between points, 250km buffer calculated using EPSG:3832 projection; land defined by HDX Fiji shapefile excluding uninhabited Ceva-i-Ra. Annex 2 "Historical Analysis" — Historical Actual Tracks: since 1969/70 season, trigger conditions met by 20 TCs, return period of 2.7 years (15 met Cat4/5-within-250km criterion, 9 met Cat3-5-landfall criterion, 4 met both). Past 10 seasons (since 2013/14) triggering cyclones: Winston 2015/16, Gita 2017/18, Pola 2018/19, Harold 2019/20, Yasa 2020/21. Also on this page — "Historical RSMC Nadi Official Forecasts": based on historical 72-hr forecasts for Evan 2012/13, Harold 2019/20, Yasa 2020/21, action trigger would have activated on average 70 hours before landfall/closest pass. "Historical ECMWF Forecasts": ECMWF hindcasts (since 2006/07) show readiness trigger would activate on average 87 hours before landfall/closest pass; of 8 cyclones triggering the action trigger, readiness trigger gave advance warning for 7 (Daman 2007/08 simultaneous); 1 false alarm (Keni 2017/18); remaining 82 storms correctly not triggered.

Distribution list B table: rows for Ministry of Health & Medical Services, Ministry of Women/Children/Social Protection, Ministry of Agriculture, Ministry of Education, Ministry of Rural & Maritime Development & Disaster Management, cc NDMO — named contacts and emails.

Map and text: Annex 5 "Draft Complementary cyclone-path information messages" — sample (fabricated) email dated Thursday Oct 5 2023, Subject "Anticipatory action Fiji – Forecast information", re Cyclone Yasa forecast produced 00:00 UTC 2020-12-15; states Readiness trigger: ACTIVATED, Action trigger: ACTIVATED. Map: "RSMC Nadi forecast for Yasa 2020/2021" showing Fiji (Vanua Levu, Viti Levu, Lautoka, Suva, Eastern islands) with Official 72-hour forecast best track (black) and uncertainty cone, Unofficial 120-hour forecast best track (white) and uncertainty, colored dots along track marking Category 5 (purple) and Category 4 (red) points, and a blue "Area within 250km of Fiji" boundary circle around the archipelago. Track passes from NW through open ocean, curving southeast near/over Fiji.

--- page 27 ---
Chart: "Yasa 00:00 2020-12-15 forecast distances" — horizontal dot-and-error-bar plot of minimum distance (km) from best track forecast to each Fiji province, x-axis 0–500km, error bars = uncertainty cone. Provinces (top to bottom) with approx. distance/category-at-closest-pass (purple=Cat5, red=Cat4): Lomaiviti (Eastern) ~0km; Lau (Eastern) ~10km; Bua (Northern) ~10km; Ba (Western) ~20km; Tailevu (Central) ~20km; Ra (Western) ~30km; Macuata (Northern) ~60km; Cakaudrove (Northern) ~65km; Rewa (Central) ~65km; Naitasiri (Central) ~65km; Nadroga_Navosa (Western) ~80km; Namosi (Central) ~100km; Serua (Central) ~115km; Kadavu (Eastern) ~120km — all Category 5 at closest pass; Rotuma (Eastern) ~345km, Category 4 at closest pass, with widest error bar (~205–480km). Below chart: link to GitHub code, contact info for OCHA Centre for Humanitarian Data (Tristan Downing), address in The Hague.
